Современный григорианский календарь — пр: The modern Gregorian calendar is a profane civil system with a multi-layered history. Its months and year counting are inherited from Rome. The premises of the seven-day week go back to Ancient Babylon: Babylonian astrology attached special significance to the seven visible celestial bodies. The seven-day rhythm came to Rome along two lines - the Jewish Sabbath and the Greco-Roman planetary. In the ancient world, the days of the week received heavenly patrons - the Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus and Saturn - and so, even in ancient times, a sacred image of each day was formed. The tradition of celebrating the New Year on January 1 also came from Rome and was not invented by one person. January was associated with Janus, the god of doors, transitions and beginnings. In 153 BC. e. the consuls' assumption of office was postponed to this day so that they could go to the war in Spain earlier; Since the years were named after consuls, January 1 became the civil beginning of the year, and the reform of Julius Caesar consolidated this tradition. In 1582, Pope Gregory XIII introduced the reform named after him to correct the accumulated bias of the Julian calendar and return the vernal equinox to the church calculation of Easter. Therefore, the modern calendar combines the Babylonian-Jewish, Greco-Roman, Roman civil and Christian-ecclesiastical heritage. In the symbolic system GENESIS, the patron of this chronology is Kronos - the image of time, measure, limit and the inexorable course of cycles. Saturday is understood here as a sacred day of obligatory rest: a time to stop ordinary work, restore the body and return to inner silence. This practice is consistent with the Jewish Shabbat, the seventh day, when it is prescribed to abstain from work and dedicate the day to God.
